subject: Renewal sync: align fiscal windows & enable sprint-burst onramp
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal timing and short-term burst capacity question

Hi Evelyn,

We're reviewing the renewal coming up in February and want to explore two things: (1) aligning the renewal to our fiscal year (July 1) so we can co-term future contracts, and (2) the ability to front-load a short "sprint" of additional capacity for a product launch in Q3 while keeping multi-year pricing. Can Redwood support an early burst for 2 months with usage credits and then settle to a multi-year ramp?

Procurement asked for a straw model (term length + financial impact) so they can route internally. Can you share options and an outline of steps?

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Park
Sr. Platform Manager, Acme Health

Attachment: ACME_Renewal_Questionnaire.pdf (pdf)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal timing and short-term burst capacity question

Sam — thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely support what you're describing. High-level options below; I attached a one-pager with numbers.

Options (quick overview):
- 24-month multi-year with fiscal alignment (July 1 start): up-front commit for predictable unit pricing + annual true-up.
- Sprint-burst addendum: 2-month pre-paid burst bucket (guaranteed capacity) that burns down first; unused portion can be applied as credit against year 1 usage.
- Hybrid: 36-month contract with graduated ramp (year 1 conservative, year 2+ larger) + shorter-term burst credit to cover Q3 launch.

Operational notes / steps:
1) We prepare a renewal summary and redline showing the sprint addendum language (for procurement/legal) — take 2 business days.
2) If you want co-term to July 1, we'll pro-rate the remaining months and propose a transition credit to smooth the change.
3) Marissa will share pricing ladders; Ben will coordinate billing cadence and invoice samples for procurement.

Next actions: which of the three options would you like a formal quote for? If you want the sprint in July/Aug, tell us target start date and expected peak QPS or token volume.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
VP, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachment: ACME_Renewal_Summary_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Acme Health — structure recommendation for sprint-burst + fiscal align

Team — quick internal note so we have a single ask back to Acme. Sam is leaning toward a 24-month co-term to July 1 but needs a 2-month sprint-burst in Q3 (peak: ~2.5x baseline token usage). Procurement will want clean language on credits and pro-ration.

My recommended approach (to present formally):
- Offer a 24-month term starting July 1 (co-term), with year 1 commit equal to 1.25x their current run-rate to encourage early onboarding.
- Add a "Sprint Addendum": pre-paid 2-month burst bucket charged at a discounted overage rate (e.g., 60% of list overage) with any unused funds credited to their year-1 committed usage.
- Include an auto-renew opt-in clause with 60-day notice to opt-out (procurement prefers predictable renewals but wants flexibility).
- Provide invoice examples: (a) pro-rated transition invoice for July 1 start, (b) sprint addendum invoice delivered 30 days before sprint start.

Notes and asks for pricing/legal:
- Marissa: produce two quote variants (A = 24m standard commit + sprint; B = 36m with lower unit price + sprint credit). Include list vs net and sample true-up language.
- Ben: confirm billing cadence and whether we can put sprint bucket on a separate line item for ease of procurement. Also confirm whether we can issue a transition credit on first invoice.
- Karthik: loop in contracts to draft the sprint addendum and the short auto-renew clause.

I attached my summary for context. I'm going to send this consolidated proposal to Sam after we have price variants.

Thanks — E

Attachment: acme-renewal-redline-v2.docx (docx)

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Sam Park <sam.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal timing and short-term burst capacity question

Evelyn / Team — this looks promising and aligned with procurement priorities. We reviewed your 24-month + sprint approach internally and prefer Variant A (24m co-term with sprint addendum). A few clarifications before we proceed to DocuSign:
1) Can the sprint bucket be billed 30 days in advance and be refundable as credit if less than 50% consumed?
2) Confirm the pro-rate math for moving to July 1 (we need the example for our FP&A team).
3) Please confirm the auto-renew notice window (we prefer 60 days).

Procurement is prepared to accept a DocuSign with these terms once the redline reflects the refundable credit threshold and the examples are included.

Once we have those two small changes, we can route to Finance for signature. Please send DocuSign link and invoice examples.

Thanks,
Lisa Chen
Director, Strategic Partnerships — Acme Health

Attachment: docusign_acme_renewal_link.txt (text)
